selection_rationale: CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II workload (3 sequential seeds; no GPU needed). Plan target: AMD EPYC 7B13 64-core CPU matching t0091 historical machine spec; t0091 used $0.2290/hr offer base = $0.2452/hr instance billing on machine_id 55891 (Norway, host_id 85684). Search returned 5 EPYC 7B13 offers; selected the cheapest 64-core instance: id=31574004, machine_id=55836 (Norway, host_id=85684 — same Norway host as t0091's machine 55891), 64 effective cores (128 logical SMT2), 252 GB RAM, 743 GB disk, public_ipaddr 141.0.85.201, 407-day duration, reliability 0.9973, dph_total=$0.1490/hr (offer base; instance billing is $0.16519/hr including storage). This is 35% cheaper than t0091's $0.2290/hr base — same EPYC 7B13 64-core silicon, same Norway host fleet, slightly different machine_id but identical microarchitecture. Estimated 6-10h sequential 3-seed wall-clock at $0.16519/hr = $0.99-$1.65 total instance cost. The $3.15 task budget cap and per-seed $1.00 watchdog give comfortable headroom. Reliability 0.9973 sits below the 0.995 threshold for 5-24h jobs but above 0.98 for 1-5h jobs; per-seed wall-clock is ~2-3h so each seed is in the 1-5h bracket where 0.99 reliability is acceptable, and t0091 successfully ran 2.6h on the sister machine 55891 from this same Norway host fleet at reliability 0.9967 (lower than this offer's 0.9973). NSGA-II saves a per-generation checkpoint (results/data/nsga2_checkpoint.json union pattern from t0091/t0083) so a mid-run host failure costs at most one generation, not the whole seed. The single bundled RTX 5060 Ti GPU is idle (gpu_verified=false; cpu_verified=true is the t0080/t0091-style success criterion). Two cheaper EPYC 7B13 alternatives existed in Texas at $0.6674-$0.8014/hr (4-5x more expensive — multi-GPU offers padding the dph_total) and one California machine at $2.1361-$4.2694/hr (multi-GPU 4090); none competitive with the Norway $0.1490/hr offer.

Vast.ai SSH proxy auto-attaches a tmux session on TTY logins. Disabled for this instance via 'touch /root/.no_auto_tmux' through an interactive ssh -tt session piping commands via stdin (printf 'touch /root/.no_auto_tmux
ls -la /root/.no_auto_tmux
exit
' | ssh -tt ...), after which non-TTY 'ssh root@ssh9.vast.ai -p 12908 <cmd>' works for stdin-piped commands. The implementation step can SSH directly with 'ssh -i C:/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 12908 root@ssh9.vast.ai'. Public IP is 141.0.85.201 (sister of t0091's 141.0.85.200 on the same Norway EPYC 7B13 host fleet, host_id 85684); the ssh*.vast.ai proxy hostname differs (ssh9 here vs ssh4 for t0091) because Vast.ai routes proxy hostnames per instance.
